---
id: "smk-03"
title: "The Danube"
---

The Danube is the second-longest river in Europe. It rises in the Black Forest of Germany, where two small streams meet at Donaueschingen, and flows generally south-east for about 2,850 kilometres before emptying into the Black Sea through a broad delta shared by Romania and Ukraine. The river passes through or along the borders of ten countries and touches four capital cities: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade. Its drainage basin covers more than 800,000 square kilometres and includes major tributaries such as the Inn, the Drava, the Tisza and the Sava. The Danube has been an important trade route since antiquity; the Roman frontier followed its course for centuries, and today a canal links it to the Rhine so that barges can travel from the North Sea to the Black Sea. The river supports hydroelectric plants, irrigation and fisheries, and its delta is a wetland of international importance for birds.
